Exercises

Problems to check your understanding of this chapter. The solutions are folded away — try them yourself first.

Easy

1Easy

In an economy with ☕ coffee at 222, 🍞 bread at 444, and pay of 100100100, the coffee price alone quadruples to 888.

Find coffee and bread consumption, the price index, and real income.

  • A Price Is a Ratio; the Price Level Is a Level
Show solution

  1. Coffee always takes half of income, so quadrupling its price quarters the quantity: x1=0.5⋅100/8=6.25x_1 = 0.5 \cdot 100 / 8 = 6.25x1​=0.5⋅100/8=6.25 cups. Bread spending is still half of income, so x2=0.5⋅100/4=12.5x_2 = 0.5 \cdot 100 / 4 = 12.5x2​=0.5⋅100/4=12.5 loaves, unchanged.

  2. The price index re-prices the base basket (252525 cups, 12.512.512.5 loaves): (8⋅25+4⋅12.5)/100=2.5(8 \cdot 25 + 4 \cdot 12.5) / 100 = 2.5(8⋅25+4⋅12.5)/100=2.5, an index of 250250250.

    Real income is 100/2.5=40100 / 2.5 = 40100/2.5=40.

    One good's price jumping alone still lifts the price level and cuts real income — a relative-price change and a level rise rolled into one.

Medium

2Medium

A country's money supply grows at 8%8\%8% a year, real output at 2%2\%2% a year, and velocity is constant.

(1) What is inflation?

(2) Where is the price level (starting at 100100100) after 555 years?

(3) What happens to real money balances?

  • The Equation of Exchange and Neutrality
Show solution

  1. (1) Inflation is money growth minus the share absorbed by real growth: π=8−2=6%\pi = 8 - 2 = 6\%π=8−2=6%.

  2. (2) Prices multiply by 1.061.061.06 each year: P(5)=100⋅1.065≈133.8P(5) = 100 \cdot 1.06^5 \approx 133.8P(5)=100⋅1.065≈133.8.

  3. (3) Real balances M/PM / PM/P grow at roughly 2%2\%2% a year, since money grows at 8%8\%8% and prices at 6%6\%6% — exactly, 100⋅(1.08/1.06)5≈109.8100 \cdot (1.08 / 1.06)^5 \approx 109.8100⋅(1.08/1.06)5≈109.8 after 555 years. With velocity constant, M/P=Y/VM / P = Y / VM/P=Y/V, so real balances have no choice but to grow alongside real output.
